headline: High: shared filesystem plus Mentat’s broad write/network defaults create prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks when paired with Argo Workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can expose artifacts and parameters, while Mentat reads/writes files and shares state via filesystem. That creates a plausible bridge where content from Argo-managed files can be treated as instructions by Mentat. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are written into a workspace that Mentat reads
IF Mentat parses file contents as actionable instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate Argo artifact directories from Mentat workspaces
Add a manual review step before Mentat consumes generated files
Prefix generated files with non-executable markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between workflow outputs and coding assistant inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, and Mentat reads selected files while sending prompts to a configured model provider. If both operate on the same workspace, file contents can flow from Argo-managed outputs into Mentat’s third-party inference path. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree
IF Argo artifacts include sensitive parameters or secrets
IF Mentat forwards those files into its model-provider context
mitigations: Keep sensitive artifacts outside Mentat’s input paths
Restrict Mentat to explicitly selected files only
Redact parameters before workflow handoff
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation or per-agent mounts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo can interact with APIs and network egress, while Mentat can write and modify git state and shares state via filesystem across instances. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits and state changes can collide without locking. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles, so the conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF Argo and Mentat target the same repository or working directory
IF Mentat instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer per workspace
Use separate branches or directories per agent
Add a lock file before git or filesystem writes
Review diffs before applying Mentat changes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce artifacts and parameters that Mentat may read as file inputs, and Mentat’s workflow is diff-based edit proposals. That makes it plausible for Argo output to become authoritative input for downstream code edits without verification. The pair does not show automatic execution, so the blast radius is bounded below high.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes Argo-generated artifacts as source material
IF the operator applies Mentat diffs without independent review
mitigations: Require human review of all generated diffs
Annotate workflow outputs as untrusted inputs
Compare proposed edits against original sources
Limit Argo outputs to non-authoritative summaries
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream edits

E_compliance.rationale: Argo’s profile shows artifacts and parameters, while Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: sensitive code or parameters could be exposed to a third-party model provider if the same workspace is used. The evidence is insufficient for a higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in files Mentat sends to its model provider
IF retention or residency requirements apply to those files
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Mentat inputs
Use a local or approved model provider
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency controls
